reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right running against the Client, so silence is at least as favourable as the preferred position.
No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is identical to the original text and no comment was issued, which is correct here.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a heuristic false signal: the pattern cannot match because there is no audit clause to cap, and inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters would concede an audit right the Client does not currently owe.

The two Vendor-side access items are correctly characterised as non-audit: S 8(f) anti-spam measures operate on TrueLink's hosted environment, and S 9 access is at Client's request for Y2K repairs at TrueLink's cost — neither is remote or direct access to Client systems, so the walk-away trigger is absent.

Information flows cited (S 3(e) real-time usage statistics/log access to Client; S 6 supporting documentation and right to contest charges) run in the Client's favour and are properly not treated as Vendor audit hooks.
The residual caveat about unfilled fee blanks and unextracted Exhibits A and B is appropriately flagged rather than overstated, and does not undermine the compliant conclusion on the available text.
